articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Image Segmentation Techniques in Mammograms (Otsu Thresholding, FCM, and U-Net)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This study aims to employ three image segmentation techniques—Thresholding (Otsu's method), Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) clustering, and the U-Net deep learning model-on mammographic images. By assessing these methods, we seek to identify the most effective approach for different types of mammographic data and provide insights into their practical applications in clinical settings. Pre-processing steps included image conversion, grayscale transformation, median filtering, histogram equalization, and region of interest (RoI) cropping based on given coordinates. Each method's performance was evaluated using the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC). The results showed that U-Net achieved the highest accuracy, with DSC scores of 0.84 for benign and 0.81 for malignant images. These findings suggest that U-Net provides the most accurate segmentation, closely matching the ground truth annotations. Additionally, U-Net's ability to learn and represent complex features, its robustness to variations in image quality. However, U-Net is computationally intensive and requires substantial computational resources for training and inference. Followed by Otsu's method, while simpler and effective for images with clear intensity separations, is limited by global thresholding approach, which may not perform well on images with subtle variations despite noise reduction by median filtering. FCM, although capable of handling overlapping intensities, requires careful parameter tuning to achieve optimal results. This study underscores the importance of selecting and optimizing segmentation methods based on specific imaging data characteristics and preprocessing techniques, ultimately contributing to more reliable and accurate breast cancer detection (benign and malignant).

articleTitle: Developing IoT-LoRaWAn Ambulance Tracking System to Enhance Emergency Response
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Emergencies pose a significant threat to individual lives and societal stability, necessitating prompt intervention to prevent escalation. Ambulances, serving as medical transport vehicles from hospitals, are essential for transferring sick or injured patients to healthcare facilities for further treatment. The effectiveness of these crucial ambulance services can be enhanced through Internet of Things (IoT) technology. This study presents a design for an loT-Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRa WAN)-based ambulance tracking system. Leveraging LoRaWAntechnology offers an extended communication range. The system integrates a Global Positioning System (GPS) sensor with a microcontroller to track the ambulance's location. GPS data is transmitted via LoRa to a gateway, which then forwards the data to a cloud server for display in an application. Accuracy tests involved comparing GPS readings from the microcontroller-integrated system with Google Maps data. Results indicate an average error of 0.00055736% for latitude and 0.000015648% for longitude coordinates. Additionally, the developed smartphone application displays real-time GPS data with an average delay of 22 seconds.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 256 Splitter Ratio for XGS-PON FTTH Network in an Urban Area
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The demand for Internet network services will continue to grow as the population increases. With this growth, there is a greater need for increased bandwidth. This paper discusses a proposed design of an XGS-PON (10 Gigabit Symmetrical Passive Optical Network) FTTH access network for Pesona Kahuripan 3, Bogor, West Java, including calculations and analysis of the link power budget, rise time budget, BER, and Q factor to assess the viability of the proposed design. The design considers a cascade of high split ratios in ODC and ODP to increase user capacity. The result shows that the proposed FTTH design achieved all parameters in splitter ratio 1:256 with the received power of -24.090 dBm and -23.803 dBm for uplink and downlink, respectively, higher than the minimum required value of -29 dBm. The rise time system for uplink is 0.264 ns, and for downlink it is 0.265 ns, which is lower than the NRZ requirement value of 0.7 ns. BER for upstream is 2.93 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup>, and for downstream it is 2.274 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-18</sup>, which is lower than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup>. These results indicate that the proposed network can be implemented using a high splitting ratio of 1:256.

articleTitle: Identification of Non-Vehicle and Vehicle Density at Intersections Based on GPS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This study aims to identify the density of vehicles and non-vehicles at the Zero Point Yogyakarta intersection based on GPS data. The data in this study comes from one of the telecommunication operator companies in Indonesia with active MPD data criteria. The data was collected from telecommunication service users who consciously activated their location services, during the period from November 2021 to January 2022. Zero-Point Intersection in Yogyakarta was chosen because of its high density, historical value, and location in the center of Yogyakarta and as a tourist destination. In this study, GPS data was processed, using a rules-based approach to categorize users into vehicle and non-vehicle groups based on speed, distance, mobility time, and duration of time at the intersection. The results of the analysis show that the highest density occurred in November 2021, with a higher number of vehicles and non-vehicles during the day than at night. The decrease in density was seen in December 2021 and continued until January 2022, due to movement restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic. The data shows that the number of nonvehicle users is higher than that of vehicles, especially during the day. The rule-based method used in this study succeeded in distinguishing between vehicles and non-vehicles, as well as providing an understanding of mobility patterns at the Zero Point intersection in Yogyakarta. The study shows that the use of GPS technology and rule-based data analysis can enhance ongoing research on traffic management efficiency in congested urban areas.

articleTitle: Classification of DGA Botnet Detection and Their Families Using LSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Botnets represent a significant threat to network security, capable of initiating denial of service (DoS) attacks and spreading malware and spam on a large scale. Botnet evolved by using Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) to avoid sinkholing, blacklisting, and evading security systems. DGA-based botnets are capable of producing a large number of pseudo-random domains and selecting a subset to communicate with via the Command and Control (C&C) server. Several LSTM-based botnet detection approaches have been proposed. Differing from previous studies, this study proposes LSTM with an attention layer and a two-stage classification process to maximize feature extraction from the DGA and address the complexity of the DGA family and imbalance sample. The experimental results demonstrate that the model can detect botnets from a domain with precision, recall, F1, and accuracy scores of 0.9905, 0.9894, 0.9899, 0.9901 respectively. These scores indicate that the model performs well in botnet classification.

articleTitle: Automatic Calculation and Detection of Fish Maturity Levels Using Imagery and CNN Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Fish consumption in Indonesia is still relatively low compared to other countries. This is unfortunate, especially considering how much fish nutrition influences health. To overcome the problem of low consumption of marine fish due to its relatively high price, efforts are needed to develop freshwater fish. However, human population growth, climate change, and unsustainable fishing practices have placed enormous pressure on fisheries resources in the region. Biomass estimation in aquaculture can be done with the basic operation of counting fish. It is important to encourage more efficient breeding and sensible feeding. Fish counting is a reference for determining survival rates, regulating breeding density, and marketing transportation management. This helps farmers in accurately estimating production potential and calculating reproduction rates. Most freshwater aquaculture in the region currently uses labor-intensive or destructive fish counting techniques. This takes a lot of time, is prone to mistakes, and can easily harm the fish's body. So we need a technique that can count fish automatically, precisely, and effectively. Technology makes it possible to take digital images of fish quickly and without damaging fish populations. This approach is important because of its high efficacy, affordability, and simplicity of use. To identify and count the number of fish, convolutional neural networks (CNN) will be used in this investigation. Underwater fish image processing technology presents significant challenges due to the complex underwater environment resulting in changing lighting conditions. It is known that the CNN algorithm has an average calculation and detection accuracy rate of 94.27% based on evaluation results.

articleTitle: Development of an Internet of Things-Based Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System for Wastewater Monitoring on the Communal Wastewater Treatment Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The wastewater parameters should be monitored regularly to maintain the quality in the range of allowed standard. A real-time wastewater monitoring system is required for effective monitoring. This paper presents an implementation of Internet of Things (IoT)-based Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) for wastewater monitoring in the communal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). The proposed system adopts the Haiwell Human Machine Interface (HMI) as the SCADA system and integrates it with the IoT platform. To evaluate the proposed SCADA, the WWTP Simulator is developed to model the wastewater parameters, implement them on the embedded modules, and communicate with the HMI using WiFi. The experimental results show that the real-time monitoring, historical data, and alarm features work appropriately and offer benefits for wastewater monitoring and analysis. Further, the performance of Modbus Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocols used for communication between HMI and WWTP Simulator is compared, where the data delivery ratio of the Modbus TCP and MQTT protocols is 99.03% and 99.78%, respectively.

Author Keywords: Internet of Things (IoT)-based Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)

articleTitle: Design of Clinical Thermometer Calibration Instrument Based on PID System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: A body temperature thermometer is a measuring equipment that must be calibrated periodically according to a specific standard. An extensively employed media for calibrating thermometers in the present day is one that requires a considerable amount of time to reach a stable temperature. The objective of developing this tool is to incorporate PID controls to minimize measurement errors and achieve a more stable and rapid temperature control for calibrating the thermometer. To achieve this, one must assess and analyze the impact of temperature stability on the calibration media of the thermometer, as well as examine the heating elements and temperature sensors of the LM35. The study employs a minimal system for data processing, utilizing the PID system as a temperature controller for the heating element. The LM-35 sensor is used as the temperature sensor, the flashlight serves as the heating medium, and the LCD is used for display purposes. The measurements were conducted at temperatures of 37°C, 39°C, and 41°C. The thermohygrometer measurements were compared to a calibration device, resulting in an average error or difference of 0.27°C at a temperature setting of 37 °C, 0.31°C at a temperature setting of 39 °C, and 0.33°C at a temperature setting of 41 °C. This indicates that the temperature variation at each location is lower than the average of 1 °C.

articleTitle: Radiosonde System Using ESP32 and LoRa Ra-02 Web-Based for Upper-Air Profile Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: A Study about upper air profile observation, weather forecasting and atmosphere observation is very important information for all people, as it can support or inhibit human activities process that involve measuring and analyzing atmospheric parameters such as temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind speed at various heights above the earth's surface for fields that are related to weather and climate. One of the instruments used to measure weather parameters for the upper air profile is the radiosonde. Radiosonde is a system consisting of a transmitter and receiver where the transmitter or receiver system consists of a temperature, humidity, and air pressure sensor that is equipped with GPS carried by a balloon to the atmosphere, then the data of the observations is transmitted to the observation station. However, the radiosonde system is quite costly. The background was what created the idea for the author to make a low-cost radiosonde system. In this research, we make radiosonde system using the ESP32 microcontroller, DHT 22 and BMP 180 sensors to measure temperature, humidity, air pressure, and altitude and Neo-Blox 6M GPS for navigational and tracking of longitude and latitude. The data will be transmitted via the implementation of LoRa (Long Range) antenna modules. The observation data will then be processed in the database and shown in real time on the website. Several experiments have produced positive results, thus providing incentives for further improvements and applications in the field of meteorology.

articleTitle: A Digital Evidence Analysis of the Twinme Application on Android Based on INTERPOL Guidelines for Digital Forensics Laboratories
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The Twinme application on Android (referred to as Twinme) is one of the Instant Messaging applications that uses end-to-end encryption in communication. The ever-evolving security features of this application can be misused by criminals to protect themselves from being monitored by authorities. For example, a criminal can exploit Twinme by using an alias when involved in a drug trafficking network. Handling this kind of problem requires the role of digital forensics to provide information to investigators in finding digital evidence. This study aims to conduct an analysis of digital evidence on Twinme in a test environment of an Android smartphone version 11 in a rooted condition. The selection of the Android operating system is based on its widespread use worldwide. There are three scenarios used: normal usage of the application, manual deletion, and the disappearing message feature. This study adapts the INTERPOL guidelines to examine digital evidence from Twinme usage, tailored to the device used. The artifacts found can then be reconstructed into digital evidence and analyzed to extract additional usage information. This information can be valid digital evidence in cases of criminal activity, contributing to the overall forensic process and helping in building a legal case. The analysis results show that even though Twinme has a mechanism for deleting messages, both manually and automatically, proper digital forensic techniques can still reveal significant digital artifacts. Therefore, applications such as Twinme remain vulnerable to forensic analysis that can reveal evidence in the context of criminal investigations.

Author Keywords: INTERPOL Global Guidelines For Digital Forensics Laboratories

articleTitle: Analysis of Comparison Faster R-CNN Backbone for Oil Palm Tree Counting using Drone Imagery Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The palm oil industry is an important subsector in the Indonesian economy. Counting the number of oil palm trees using drone imagery is crucial in developing efficient strategies for managing oil palm plantations. This research aims to compare the effectiveness of two Faster R-CNN models with ResNet50 and VGG16 backbones for detecting and counting the number of oil palm trees in high-resolution images captured by drones at PTPN IV's oil palm plantations in Gunung Banyu, North Sumatra. The model was trained and tested, and its performance was measured regarding recall, accuracy, and F1 Score. The results of the comparative analysis show that the Faster R-CNN model with the VGG 16 backbone shows high accuracy, namely between 97-99%, while the results for the ResNet50 backbone do not exceed 95%. These accuracy results may be due to the VGG16 architecture being simpler and suited to the data set used. At the same time, ResNet50 requires better parameter adjustments or more significant data to achieve optimal performance. This study is relevant for choosing the right Faster R-CNN backbone to help count oil palm trees in managing plantations better and more efficiently.

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare: IoT-LoRaWAN System for Stress Level Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Indonesia is grappling with a significant mental health issue as the number of suicides continues to rise each year. This phenomenon aligns with the global trend highlighted by the World Health Organization (WHO), which reports approximately 700,000 suicides occurring worldwide annually. Impaired mental health frequently plays a significant role in cases of suicide. Thus, prioritizing mental well-being is crucial in preventing suicide. Experiencing high levels of stress can significantly worsen one's mental well-being. In order to address the issue at hand, we require a creative approach to monitoring stress levels. This research project focuses on designing and building a stress level monitoring system using IoT-LoRa Wantechnology. The system is capable of monitoring patient stress levels in real-time. Based on the test results, it is evident that the system has achieved an impressive average accuracy of 97% in monitoring stress levels over 20 data collection times. We conducted a thorough analysis to evaluate the precision of the data obtained from the sensor by comparing it with a pulse oximeter.

articleTitle: Analysis of Music Genre Based on Similar Audio Features Using K-Means Algorithm: A Case of Spotify Top Hits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The culture of listening to music has become a part of people's daily lives. The music revolution has happened since it was first invented, along with the rapid growth of technology. The changes include the emergence of various latest music genres and the availability of music platforms that make it easier for humans to consume and interact with music. The availability of digital music service platforms also makes it easier for music industry players to experiment with music. Spotify is one of the most widely used digital music platforms by the global community. The amount of music provided reaches tens of millions, including various singers, types, and genres. The increasing diversity of music widely circulated today is irrelevant to be labeled with certain genre-dividing lines. Many new pieces of music have emerged by utilizing technology to create music with diverse and characteristic audio features. Because of this problem, researchers needed to cluster music genres based on similar audio features. Data collection was conducted on the Spotify music platform by clustering data on Spotify Top Hits to find out the audio features of music that are most popular with the public. The K-Means method is used because it is suitable and has a very high accuracy rate of 90%. The results show that music with tempo audio features and a music scale has become the most accepted music genre by the public.

articleTitle: Training Critical Thinking and Collaboration for Young People with the Help of Video Games
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This study explores the development and usability evaluation of a cooperative puzzle-genre video game aimed at enhancing critical thinking, problem-solving, and cooperative skills in young people. Despite the common perception of video games as detrimental, they can also be educational. Usability was assessed using the Keyboard and Mouse Game Usability Questionnaire (KM-GUQ), which evaluates Easiness, Learnability, Challenges, Efficiency, and Satisfaction. The Mann-Whitney U test results showed no statistically significant differences in usability perceptions between frequent and rare players of cooperative games, with both groups median scores ranging from 4.0 to 4.5, The results suggest that the interface is equally easy to control, understand, and adapt to, as well as similarly challenging and satisfying, for both groups. Overall, the findings suggest that the usability of the application interface is consistent across users with different levels of experience in playing cooperative video games.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Image Enhancement Techniques for Improving Skin Cancer Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Skin cancer is a noncontagious but dangerous disease characterized by its ferocity and speed to spread to other parts of the body, causing death for the sufferers. Indonesia is a tropical climate country with extremely high sun exposure, which is a significant contributing factor to the development of skin malignancy. Melanoma is the most common skin cancer in Indonesia, reaching 1,609 cases in 2020. Manual detection of skin cancer relies heavily on the skills of observers, raising the possibility of errors. This study utilized three classes of skin cancer: melanoma, nevus, and seborrheic keratosis. Two kinds of noise were employed: Salt and Pepper and Gaussian. The results of the noisy images underwent processing to determine the most effective filter for all noise types. The Gaussian filter depicted better performance in reducing noise, especially Salt and Pepper noise. However, both the average filter and the Gaussian filter exhibited similar performance in reducing Gaussian noise.

articleTitle: Comic-Based Approach on Dark Pattern in Cookies Disclaimer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Cookies on a website are basically text-based files whose purpose is to store sensitive data. However, cookie disclaimers often use ambiguous words, so that users do not know what to do, which illustrates the existence of a dark pattern in consent. Dark pattern is a design impulse that directs people's behavior through persuasive interface design with positive results from implementing comics or images based on previous research. This research uses a comic-based method that is applied to a cookie disclaimer on a website by comparing the effectiveness of the comic-based cookie disclaimer with the text-based cookie disclaimer. The results of this research found that as many as 80% of people chose the “ignore” button on comic-based content, while 20% on text-based content.

articleTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Indonesia Non-Convention Vessel Standards Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: One factor in ship accidents is violation of regulations. Indonesia has passed regulations for shipping in the form of the NCVS (Non-Convention Vessel Standards) Indonesia book. The problem with the book is that it contains a plethora of information and is difficult to access although it was meant to be utilized by the public. The Indonesian government provides a comprehensive legal database, but navigating it is still complicated and overly complex. Considering the points mentioned, we see a potential to implement Natural Language Processing methods for assisting in the publication, navigation, and exploration of the NCVS Indonesia book. In this paper, we developed a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) model which involves retrieving relevant sections of the NCVS Indonesia book based on the user's query and generating responses that are supported factually by the NCVS Indonesia book based on the retrieved context. The retrieval component of the RAG model achieved promising evaluation scores when retrieving the top 7 documents with recall@k of 0.8889, precision@k of 0.8095, and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of 0.3521. Evaluation results suggests that our model strikes a good balance between retrieving relevant documents and avoiding irrelevant ones specifically within the top 7 documents.

articleTitle: Architecture Design for a Smart Chatbot to Enhance English Conversation Skills Using RiveScript, NLP, and ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a chatbot architecture design for K-12 English-speaking learners. English learning chatbots have many advantages, including 24/7 availability, interactive interaction, instant feedback, vocabulary training, progress measurement, and effective repetition. Key technologies commonly used to build learning chatbots include natural language processing (NLP), artificial intelligence (AI), chatbot frameworks, and programming languages. The fact that chatbots can only respond to programming and data is a drawback. Chatbot engines cannot think creatively. ChatBot also needs to provide deep insights. The learning material can adapt the necessary chatbot skills to the learning context. Chatbots must match the subject matter and conversation ethics, adjust to students' abilities, and have a knowledge base. We designed a chatbot with a unique architecture and model consisting of RiveScript, NLP, ChatGPT, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech converters to meet this need. This combination results in a chatbot that can communicate with students according to the learning context.

articleTitle: Segmentation for Lenke Scoliosis X-Ray Images Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Lenke is a classification of spinal deformities first discovered by Dr. Lwrence G. Lenke, and since then, new classification systems have been used to assess the severity of scoliosis. According to Lenke's classification criteria, scoliosis is divided into 6 types, namely type 1 to type 6. In reading the severity of scoliosis, doctors make observations through X-Ray images. This method takes time and is tiring to find out in detail the type and diagnose existing disorders. This can cause observation results to be inaccurate and allow misdiagnosis to occur. Currently, several studies have been carried out to develop machine learning technology for Lenke scoliosis classification based on machine learning. The stage that determines the ease of classification is segmentation to separate objects from their background, making it easier for doctors to determine existing abnormalities. Segmentation in Lenke scoliosis types 1–5 is still a great opportunity for development. In this research we will segment X-Ray images of Lenke scoliosis types 1–5 using machine learning, namely Thresholding and Active Contour. By comparing the visual results and the Dice Coefficient, Precision, Recall and Standard Deviation metrics, the research shows that the segmentation method active contour is slightly better than the threshold method.

articleTitle: History Leap: Enhancing Historical Learning Through a Game-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The development of “History Leap: Indonesian Independence” integrates engaging 2D platformer gameplay with historical narratives to stimulate dwindling interest in Indonesian history. The game's urgency lies in addressing the decreasing engagement with traditional history education, making it vital to innovate educational methods. Our research utilizes a game development approach, specifically the Agile methodology, to create an educational game that elucidates Indonesia's journey to independence. Participants, including university and high school students, played the game and evaluated its educational impact. The results showed significant satisfaction with the game's learning effectiveness and enjoyment, despite lower scores in game presence. These findings were analyzed using T-Test and Mann-Whitney methods based on the data normality. This underscores the potential of game-based learning to enhance historical education across different educational stages.

articleTitle: Predicting Age and Gender Across Different Races Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Age and gender are two important attributes possessed by humans that serve as their identity in social life. Faking age and gender are criminal acts that are harmful especially for bad purposes. Therefore, artificial intelligence systems are needed which can predict the age and gender of humans with high accuracy. The model commonly used to detect images and perform visual-based tasks is CNN. Nowadays, there are many frameworks and other models that are the development of CNN models, one of them is DeepFace. The purpose of this research is to evaluate the CNN model and compare its accuracy with DeepFace using Mean Absolute Error metric for age and Exact Match Ratio metric for gender. The test data used is divided into 5 races, namely Asian, Black, Indian, White, and other races (like Middle Eastern, Latino, and Hispanic). The result of this research is the accuracy value for each race using CNN and DeepFace which states that DeepFace is superior for age prediction and CNN is superior for gender prediction.

articleTitle: CrashEventLLM: Predicting System Crashes with Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: As the dependence on computer systems expands across various domains, focusing on personal, industrial, and large-scale applications, there arises a compelling need to enhance their reliability to sustain business operations seamlessly and ensure optimal user satisfaction. Achieving enhanced reliability depends on predicting and preemptively addressing these failures presents a formidable challenge. However, the challenge of predicting failures and mitigate them in timely manner is a complex problem. Thus, it becomes important to adopt effective strategies for managing failures and minimizing their impact. System logs generated by these devices serve as valuable repositories of histori-cal trends and past failures. The use of machine learning techniques for failure prediction has become commonplace, enabling the extraction of insights from past data to anticipate future behavior patterns. Recently, large language models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tasks including summarization, reasoning, and event prediction. Therefore, in this paper, we endeavor to investigate the potential of large language models in predicting system failures, leveraging insights learned from past failure behavior to inform reasoning and decision-making processes effectively. Our approach involves leveraging data from the Intel® Computing Improvement Program (ICIP) system crash logs to identify significant events and develop CrashEventLLM. This model, built upon a large language model framework, serves as our foundation for crash event prediction. Specifically, our model utilizes historical data to forecast future crash events, informed by expert annotations. Additionally, it goes beyond mere prediction, offering insights into potential causes for each crash event. This work provides the preliminary insights into prompt-based large language models for the log-based event prediction task.

articleTitle: Mobile Puzzle Game Paper Prototype to Learn Hangul Writing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Korean language becomes popular as the result of the Hallyu Wave. However, the language uses Hangul writing and its uniqueness makes it more challenging to master. Many learning media have been developed to help learn Hangul writing. However, media focusing on learning how to properly form the syllable blocks in Hangul is still scarce. We argue that puzzle games can be a potential solution to the problem. To examine the game's feasibility, we created a paper prototype and conducted a testing session with participants with basic Hangul reading skills. The participants were asked to play the paper prototype and were interviewed about the game's enjoyability and how they compared their experience with similar learning media. From the test, we found that puzzle games can be an enjoyable method to learn Hangul writing that specifically focuses on the rules to form the syllable blocks.

articleTitle: VGG19-Based Neural Style Transfer for Data Augmentation in Lung Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Deep learning models have shown promising results in computational pathology, but their high data demand poses challenges for multiinstitutional data collaborations due to privacy concerns. Federated learning offers a novel approach to collaboratively train models across different sites without sharing private data. However, imbalanced data distributions among participating sites can lead to performance degradation and instability in federated learning. This study proposes a federated version of the neural style transfer algorithm, originally introduced by Gatys et al., as a data augmentation technique for highly class-imbalanced lung cancer imaging datasets. The proposed method involves selecting characteristic style images and generating gram style matrices at local sites, which are then transferred to other imbalanced sites without leaking any private data. This technique aims to augment the underrepresented classes and mitigate the effects of data imbalance. The proposed method utilizes the VGG19 architecture, a powerful convolutional neural network, as the backbone for feature extraction and style transfer, leveraging its deep layers to capture both content and style information effectively. The approach was evaluated on a federated learning configuration using a lung cancer imaging dataset from multiple institutions.

articleTitle: Innovations in Computational IntelligenceAutomated IoT-Based Smart Plant Watering System For Revolutionizing Plant Care
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes an IoT-based plant watering system innovation to revolutionise plant care. This study concentrates on advancements in automated IoT-based technology to address the need for an upgraded plant watering system. Previous research focused primarily on plant and water quality aspects, neglecting a comprehensive monitoring approach. Traditional manual watering schedules lacked real-time monitoring, presenting environmental challenges. The system provides a detailed display of soil conditions and humidity levels on an LCD using an Arduino UNO for soil moisture, humidity, and ultrasonic sensor. Additionally, water level data is accessible via the ESP8266 module via the Blynk application. The proposed innovations aim to significantly improve environmental sustainability, reduce risks, and improve plant condition monitoring efficiency.

articleTitle: Automated Smart City Planning through Personalized Large Language Model with Retrieval Augmented Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The rapid urbanization and the need for sustainable city management have driven the demand for intelligent and efficient smart city planning solutions. This paper explores an innovative approach to automated smart city planning using a personalized large language model (LLM) combined with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). Our proposed system leverages the personalized mistral7b model, enabling the ingestion and analysis of multiple documents, including smart city master plans and government regulations. This methodology ensures tailored urban planning recommendations while maintaining data privacy by running the system locally. In light of the dangers of cyberattacks and the inherent risks associated with using foreign-run services, our approach provides a secure and autonomous solution for urban development planning.

articleTitle: Smart Garbage Monitoring System with IoT: A Solution for Overflowing Bins
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This project, a Garbage Monitoring System with IoT, represents a highly innovative solution designed to maintain cleanliness in cities by preventing the overflow of unwanted garbage. Its primary objectives are to monitor the status of garbage bins and relay information regarding the level of collected waste through specialized sensors. The system employs Arduino as its microcontroller, aiming to create an intelligent monitoring infrastructure that addresses the core issue. Utilizing ultrasonic sensors strategically positioned above the bins, the system assesses the garbage level and compares it against the depth capacity of the bins. The key components include an Arduino UNO microcontroller, an LCD screen, LEDs, IoT technology, and a buzzer. When the garbage reaches its limit, all LEDs illuminate, the buzzer activates, the LCD displays the level, and an IoT notification is dispatched as a reminder to dispose of the waste. Moreover, this system enhances its functionality by providing continuous graphical representations of bin levels via IoT, contributing significantly to urban cleanliness efforts and preventing potential overflow.

articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review of Software Estimation in Global Software Development
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Software development is always characterized by certain parameters. In the context of Global Software Development (GSD), one of the key challenges for software developers is predicting the development effort of a software system based on developer details, size, complexity, and other measures. When development teams are spread apart, it presents a number of challenges. Communication and coordination become more complex, leading to hidden costs associated with managing software development across different locations. Hence, the software estimation models used for co-located software development are not suitable for estimation in GSD. Software estimation in GSD has become a crucial area of research. This paper presents the findings of a systematic literature review on software estimation in the context of GSD, with the aim of providing researchers and practitioners with a comprehensive understanding of the current state of the art in this area. Over the last decade, only a handful of researchers have devoted their attention to estimating efforts in GSD. The results show that estimation methods in GSD have not been widely explored. The COCOMO-II method is the most widely adapted method for GSD, and Time Zone is the most agreed Cost Driver for GSD.

articleTitle: Identification of Visitors at Tourist Destinations in Yogyakarta Using GPS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This study utilized GPS data from telecommunications operators to analyze tourist behavior in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. A rule-based identification technique was developed to differentiate domestic tourist activity. The analysis revealed significant visitor pattern variations and highlighted priority destinations such as Gembira Loka and Parangtritis Beach. Preprocessing methods and rule-based classification categorized visitors into tourists (individuals from different sub-districts at tourist locations), working residents (spending 40 hours a week at tourist locations), visitors (spending an average of 3.3 hours at tourist sites), and ordinary residents (not fitting the previous categories). This study offers an essential reference for accurately assessing tourism's economic impact, emphasizing that non-local tourists contribute more significantly to local revenue through spending on accommodation, food, and attractions. The findings assist in planning visits and developing effective tourism policies. The study underscores the importance of precise visitor identification techniques to understand travel patterns and enhance tourism development. The results demonstrate GPS data's potential in tourism research, informing marketing strategies and product development. Future research could integrate additional data sources, such as social media check-ins or transaction records, to improve visitor profiling accuracy. Moreover, studies could investigate the long-term impacts of tourism on local economies and the environment. In Indonesia, working hours regulated by Law No. 13 of 2003 ensure a balance between productivity and leisure, influencing tourist behavior. This study advances the understanding of visitor behavior in Yogyakarta and promotes sustainable tourism development.

articleTitle: Development of Smart Badminton Scoring System for Educational Purpose
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)

authors.preferredName: Siti Nurul Aqmariah bt Mohd Kanafiah

abstract: The development of smart badminton scoring system for educational purposes is an innovative educational strategy for teaching badminton to all students and new athletes. This is due to the fact that many students and new athletes are unable to learn badminton by traditional instructional approaches such as reading, looking through books or conventional manual scoring method. The paperless intelligent badminton scoring system is created with two main objectives in mind. The first objective is to develop an intelligent badminton scoring system for teaching strategies, with a focus on doubles. It is impractical to expect all novices to be familiar with the rules and regulations of badminton doubles, including how to determine who serves and who receives and which side a player should be on. Second, to monitor and evaluate the performance of the scoring system in actual matches. This smart badminton scoring system was designed with IoT based so that anyone can use it and interpret it in the simplest way possible. This project created a badminton scoring kit that replicates an actual game, with a focus on doubles. Before beginning play on badminton equipment, the system can be adjusted for the start game, and players can be renamed using Blynk. Once the badminton kit has been activated, the user can control the game and the results will be recorded. In addition, all badminton match results will be generated and stored on a mobile device. The results of a match may be displayed on the user's mobile device. The results are automatically generated on a Google spreadsheet in PDF paperless form. This project has incrementally developed a badminton kit that would teach students and novice athletes while also aiding them in obtaining fundamental badminton knowledge and having fun. Additionally, the production cost of the badminton set is inexpensive, and the user can save a substantial amount of time by eliminating the need for a manual scoresheet.

articleTitle: Spatial Analysis of Traffic Congestion in Urban Areas of Jakarta, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Traffic congestion in Jakarta, Indonesia, is a significant challenge for its residents. As the capital city and economic hub, Jakarta is flooded with commute needs, resulting in a skyrocketing number of vehicles. Despite government efforts, traffic conditions remain severe, with a 4.05% increase in vehicle registrations from 2021 to 2022, totaling 21.8 million active vehicles. To tackle the problem, this study uses the theoretical framework of web-based GIS functionality for traffic detection and management. We developed a JavaScript web-based GIS application using the Google Maps API, with interactive maps, geolocation services, route planning, and real-time traffic data, calculating the Traffic Congestion Index (TCI) and assessing each journey's carbon emissions and fuel consumption. From our analysis, our model shows Jakarta's overall traffic congestion throughout the day is not excessively high. However, there are consistent specific hotspots and peak times when congestion significantly increases. Our approach demonstrates the potential of advanced GIS tools for detailed spatial analysis and effective traffic management. This comprehensive application offers valuable insights for urban planners and traffic authorities, supporting data-driven decision-making and highlighting the need for further development to enhance Jakarta's efforts in tackling traffic congestion.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Innovations in Code Generation: A Systematic Literature Review of Methods, Challenges and Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent advances in machine learning (ML) technologies applied to code generation, with a focus on literature published between 2022 and 2024. We collect and analyze 36 studies from four major publication databases: ACM, IEEE Xplore, Springer, and Scopus, highlighting the transformative impact of transformer-based models in this domain. Significant findings indicate that transformer-based models and graph neural networks (GNNs) are the best ways to understand and generate code. Exact match accuracy, BLEU, ROUGE, execution verification, and human studies are some of the evaluation methods that now provide comprehensive performance assessments. Major challenges identified include a lack of high-quality training data, high computational resource requirements, and security concerns. Recent trends emphasize the use of diverse neural network architectures, industrial project datasets, and novel evaluation methods to improve model robustness and applicability. Applications cover a wide range of paradigms, including code-to-description, description-to-code, and code-to-code, with tasks such as automated documentation and code optimization. Dataset innovations include the use of open-source repositories, competition datasets, and synthetic data to improve code structural and contextual understanding. This paper seeks to guide future research and foster additional innovations in the field by providing a thorough examination of both progress and challenges in ML-powered code generation.

articleTitle: Stunting Classification in Toddlers: Implementation and Evaluation of the Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Stunting in toddlers is a chronic nutritional issue that affects the physical and cognitive development of children, with serious long-term consequences such as reduced cognitive function and an increased risk of chronic diseases in adulthood. Therefore, early identification and prevention efforts for stunting are crucial. Classifying toddlers into categories of at-risk for stunting or not is essential to provide timely and appropriate interventions. This study employs data mining techniques using the decision tree algorithm to expedite the stunting detection process and improve the accuracy of nutritional status classification in children. The results indicate that the constructed decision tree model can classify children's nutritional status with an accuracy of 83.26%. The decision tree achieves high accuracy in classifying stunting in toddlers due to its ability to handle complex data and identify significant patterns within the data.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Implementation with DenseNet for Alzheimer's Disease Detection in MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The challenge posed by Alzheimer's disease (AD) in contemporary healthcare is significant due to its profound impact on cognitive functions. Recent progress in medical imaging and machine learning techniques offers promising avenues for early detection and diagnosis of AD, particularly through analyzing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans. This study addresses the critical need for precise AD detection by optimizing pretrained DenseNet models for AD classification in MRI images. We perform transfer learning and fine-tuning stages on the DenseNet121, DenseNet169, and DenseNet201 architectures to tune the models for AD detection. The model's performance is thoroughly evaluated using comprehensive assessment measures like as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our findings demonstrate that DenseNet169 achieves a remarkable accuracy of 99.806%, making it the top performer during the transfer learning phase. Moreover, DenseNet121 and DenseNet201 display competitive performance, showcasing the effectiveness of DenseNet architectures in neuroimaging tasks. These results underscore the potential of pretrained DenseNet models as potent tools for AD detection, providing valuable insights into enhancing diagnostic accuracy and patient care in neuroimaging-based disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Design Mechanics and Gameplay using LM-GM of a Serious Game for Preventing Smoking in Teenagers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Serious games are a potential medium for health promotion, especially for preventing smoking in adolescents. One aspect that is important to design is game mechanics and game play that are effective for the target user. This study evaluates the design mechanics and gameplay effectiveness of a serious game, “Smoverse 2,” developed to enhance preventive education on the dangers of smoking among adolescents aged 13–15 years. Utilizing the Learning Mechanics-Game Mechanics (LM-GM) model, the game was designed to balance educational content with engaging gameplay to improve learning outcomes. “Smoverse 2,” a role-playing game, was compared to “Smoverse 1,” an action-adventure game, to assess their impacts on player engagement and knowledge retention. The study involved 90 middle school students, divided into control and experimental groups, using A/B testing methodology. The Game Experience Questionnaire (GEQ) was employed to measure various dimensions of the player experience, including immersion, flow, competence, positive and negative affect, tension, and challenge. Results indicate that “Smoverse 2” significantly improves player engagement and educational effectiveness by effectively integrating entertainment aspects, thereby demonstrating the value of balancing educational content with engaging game mechanics in serious games.

articleTitle: Classification Analysis of Star Hotels in Banyumas Using the Random Forest Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Banyumas Regency is a hub for economic, social, and tourism activities in Central Java, including key cities like Purwokerto, Cilacap, Purbalingga, and Banjarnegara. Various hotels cater to tourists and business visitors, often hosting guests for multiple days. This research aims to classify hotels in Banyumas Regency by star ratings using the Random Forest machine learning algorithm. The study evaluates the algorithm's effectiveness in predicting hotel star ratings based on provided data features. The study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and relative advantages of the Random Forest algorithm in classifying star-rated hotels in Banyumas Regency. By developing this classification model, we can predict a hotel's star rating based on the provided dataset's features. The research involves data collection, preprocessing to handle missing values and normalize features, and developing a Random Forest classification model. The model's performance is assessed using accuracy, precision, Recall, and the F1 score, with results showing an accuracy of 86.2%, precision of 84.5%, Recall of 83.3%, and an F1 score of 83.8%. Key features from the dataset are analyzed and integrated into the model. Essential features of the dataset were analyzed and incorporated into the classification model. The analysis results on the classification of star-rated hotels in Banyumas Regency can be provided to relevant parties, such as local government or tourism industry players, offering insights and suggestions for further development using machine learning techniques for classifying star-rated hotels in Banyumas.

articleTitle: Classification of Occupant Position Based Ventilation in the Under-Actuated Zone Using K-Nearest Neighbor's
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: In light of the post-pandemic era, the educational landscape is evolving towards a new normal, with institutions such as Trilogy University in Jakarta reinitiating on-campus activities. The library, an essential component of the learning process, necessitates efficient air circulation management. At present, Trilogy University's library utilizes a conventional HVAC system that is manually controlled through wall-mounted buttons, without considering occupancy levels. The objective of this study is to design a system that can detect room occupancy by employing the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm. This system makes use of data collected from Wi-Fi network sensors placed on room vents, which capture signal strength (RSSI), frequency, and limit values from each Access Point (AP). A dataset comprising 90 samples was used to train the KNN model, resulting in an accuracy of 94% and an error rate of 0.05. The model's performance was further validated with 15 real-time samples, yielding 100% accuracy. The results suggest that the system can accurately detect room occupancy and effectively handle real-time data, indicating its potential for optimizing HVAC control in library settings.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Classification from CT Scan Images Using the LVQ Algorithm and GLCM Feature Extraction with Spatial Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related fatalities in Indonesia, primarily due to late-stage diagnoses. This study aims to develop a model that employs image processing to classify lung cancer from CT scan images. The system combines the Learning Vector Quantization (LVQ) algorithm with the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) feature extraction method and utilizes spatial filtering techniques such as low pass, median, and high pass filters. The LVQ algorithm effectively manages non-linear data and forms complex decision boundaries through the distribution of prototype vectors. The findings show that the median filtering technique achieved the highest accuracy of 90.14% at a GLCM angle of 0°, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing noise while maintaining crucial details for accurate classification. This suggests that the horizontal texture orientation may be more critical for analyzing lung images in this dataset.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Method to Enhance Receipt Identification in Consumer Communication Using Generative AI and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The rapid advancement in digital communication presents challenges in managing and categorizing large volumes of emails, particularly transactional receipts. This study introduces an ensemble method leveraging two sophisticated NLP technologies: the Generative Pre-trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The research began with acquiring an extensive, anonymized dataset from Circana, incorporating diverse real-world consumer data, including purchases, promotions, and e-commerce transactions across various retail sectors. The dataset analyzed subject lines, generated text, and receipt labels, reflecting genuine consumer transactions and offering insights into consumer messaging. The approach involved extracting and preprocessing subject lines and message previews from emails. The GPT-2 model was trained on clean email messages to generate text for initial analysis, enriching the contextual understanding of the dataset. Subsequently, the clean subject lines and generated text were passed to an LSTM model, leveraging its sequential data processing capabilities to accurately identify receipt-containing emails. The performance of this ensemble method was assessed on a diverse email dataset, focusing on precision, recall, F1 score, and overall accuracy in identifying receipt-containing emails. The findings indicated a significant 57.11% enhancement in detecting transactional receipts and a 3.24% reduction in misclassifying non-receipt content when applying the LSTM model to both clean subject lines and generated texts. This study showcases the potential of integrating generative AI with deep learning techniques for email classification tasks. Collaboration with Circana enabled leveraging a significant repository of authentic data, crucial for thorough research and analysis of consumer behavior and market trends.

articleTitle: Enhanced Traffic Collision Avoidance System Using Single Photon LiDAR in Aviation Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance aviation safety by integrating Single-photon Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) technology into the existing Traffic Collision Avoidance Systems (TCAS). This integration aims to address the limitations of current TCAS by providing precise 3D imaging over extensive distances. A study of data fusion using the Kalman filter algorithm is presented for TCAS and LiDAR sensors. The results indicate successful superposition for a moving 2D object. Additionally, design considerations, and cost and power analyses for the proposed system are discussed. A simulation in Python using iterative closest point (ICP) shows that comprehensive 3D point cloud acquisition is attainable. Hence, the system has the potential to enhance the safety of the aviation industry, by potentially reducing mid-air collisions (MAC).

articleTitle: Developing a Pancasila-Based Dataset for AI Applications in Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have generated significant interest in harnessing this technology to enhance educational outcomes across diverse contexts. This study explores the development of AI-powered educational tools grounded in the principles of Pancasila, Indonesia's national ideology, which emphasizes belief in the Deity, Humanity, Unity, Democracy, and Social Justice. By incorporating these values, the study aims to create culturally-responsive and socially-inclusive learning experiences that foster a sense of national identity and social harmony among Indonesian students. The methodology involves a multi-stage process, including a comprehensive review of existing literature and stakeholder consultations with educators, students, policymakers, and community leaders. The data collection strategy comprises surveys, classroom observations, and the curation of existing educational resources. The results indicate that Pancasila-based AI tools can transform the Indonesian education system by promoting national identity and social cohesion, despite challenges like algorithmic bias and the need for rigorous data validation. These findings highlight the potential of Pancasila-based AI applications to create an inclusive, equitable, and culturally-responsive education system, preparing students to become engaged and responsible citizens.

articleTitle: Enhancing Search Efficiency: Analyzing Learning Mechanisms in Metaheuristics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Metaheuristics have evolved significantly in the last few decades. Nowadays, more complex problems and essential applications are emerging, requiring more powerful metaheuristics to handle them. This article analyzes the characteristics and performance of existing metaheuristics, with particular emphasis on their learning mechanisms. Several critical aspects for improvement are identified, and several promising future research areas are recommended.

articleTitle: Roles of AI in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the healthcare landscape, introducing capabilities that span from predictive diagnostics to personalized treatment strategies. This review explores the multifaceted roles of AI within healthcare, emphasizing its application in three primary areas: descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive AI. Descriptive AI focuses on data analysis and the extraction of meaningful information from large datasets, helping in the identification of patterns and trends that enhance diagnostic and operational procedures. Predictive AI forecasts health outcomes and tailors medical interventions by utilizing advanced algorithms to analyze historical and real-time data, thereby improving the accuracy of medical assessments and disease anticipation. Prescriptive AI goes further by not only predicting outcomes but also suggesting actionable interventions tailored to individual patient needs, thus optimizing healthcare delivery and patient management. The integration of machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI technologies is thoroughly examined, highlighting their impact on improving diagnostics, patient care, and the overall efficiency of healthcare services.

articleTitle: The Roles of Hotel Industry and Travel Agents in a Scrum Team for an Integrated Halal Tourism Application Based on Android
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Tourism, including West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), is crucial in regional economic development. The COVID-19 pandemic caused a drastic decline in tourists, impacting hotel occupancy and demand for tour packages. Strategies to increase tourist visits are needed to address these challenges, focusing on the halal tourism market, which holds significant potential in NTB. The halal tourism market segment is highly significant in terms of visitor number and expenditure during travel. Digital promotion through technology is considered key to achieving this target. Therefore, developing a halal tourism application using the Scrum method will facilitate effective tourism promotion and services. Scrum is chosen for its advantages in effective team coordination, quick adaptation to changes, and active stakeholder involvement. This study examines the role of the hotel industry and travel agents in the Scrum team for the development of an integrated halal tourism application, aiming to produce an application that meets the expectations and needs of tourism stakeholders, increases tourist visits, and supports the recovery of the tourism sector in NTB. Final testing using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) method scored 4.85, indicating that the application was well-received by potential users and met their needs. These positive results highlight the important role of stakeholders, particularly from the hotel and travel agent industries, in the development process, where their involvement and feedback significantly contribute to shaping the application to meet user expectations and needs, demonstrating that active stakeholder participation is one of the keys to successful application development.

articleTitle: An 8-bit Quantized Globalization Model for Cat Skin Disease Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks and TensorFlow Lite
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Skin diseases are health issues that can be experienced by pets and potentially be transmitted from wild animals. However, current prediction systems predominantly rely on complex calculations that necessitate high computational power, making them challenging to deploy on mobile applications. Therefore, this study aims to optimize a skin disease detection system based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) using datasets from both wild and domestic cats. The quantized globalization model is a modified ResNet50 converted with TensorFlow Lite. This 8-bit quantization is necessary to develop a lightweight deep learning model that could operate on low-computational power units, such as smartphone or 8-bit edge computing devices. This study utilized a dataset comprising 343 images, categorized into six classes: five classes of diseases (abscesses, mange, ringworm, skin cancer, dermatitis) and one class for healthy skin. Next, the dataset was augmented to increase data variation and quantity. Subsequently, the dataset was trained on the ResNet-50 model and then converted to TensorFlow Lite with 8-bit integer data type. Finally, the quantized globalization model was validated using a separate 20% of the dataset. The validation results yielded an accuracy score of 0.930, a precision of 0.908, a recall of 0.902, and an F1-score of 0.903. Additionally, there was a significant 74.7% reduction in model size compared to the non-quantized version, demonstrating the efficiency and effectiveness of the quantization process in maintaining performance while substantially decreasing the computational resource requirements.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Potential for Solar Panel Development on House Roofs in West Jakarta, Indonesia Using GIS Applications and the Mask R-CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Jakarta, as a metropolitan city with the highest energy consumption per capita in Indonesia, is driven by population growth, economic development, and urbanization. Energy in Jakarta is mostly generated from fossil fuels, especially coal-fired power plants supplied by the National Electricity Company, thus contributing significantly to environmental degradation. Efforts to reduce fossil fuel consumption with new and renewable energy are urgently needed. By utilizing Indonesia's high solar radiation, this study aims to analyze the potential for developing solar panels that can be generated in West Jakarta based on rooftop detection. Object detection is carried out using the Deep Learning Mask R-CNN model by comparing the accuracy results between the ResNet 34 and ResNet 50 backbones to determine whether there is a significant difference in accuracy results. This study uses a dataset sourced from the repository of the Department of Public Works, Spatial Planning, and Defense of DKI Jakarta, Indonesia. The dataset collected consists of 479 images with a size of 256x256 pixels. The dataset is processed using the ArcGIS Pro application to detect rooftops and calculate the potential energy that can be generated in West Jakarta. The results show that the Mask R-CNN model with ResNet 50 is better at detecting roofs with an accuracy of 40% than ResNet 34 which only got an accuracy of 7.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. Thus, the potential electricity can be generated more than 6,800 MWh per year. This potential can contribute to the sustainable energy goals in West Jakarta, Indonesia.

articleTitle: A Confidence-Based Voting Classifier Ensemble for Effective Decentralized Botnet Detection in Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Botnet attacks are increasingly sophisticated and complex, threatening the security of personal data and critical infrastructure in various sectors. Both centralized and decentralized botnet attacks have become a serious threat in the digital world. Most existing research only focuses on detecting botnet activity without identifying the type of botnet. Meanwhile, detecting decentralized botnet attacks is a major challenge due to their stealthy nature and ability to obscure their activities in network traffic. Therefore, this research proposes a multi-faceted method using ensemble voting techniques to detect the presence of decentralized botnets. The method begins with data preprocessing and architecture analysis to ensure its quality and understand its structure. Next, an ensemble model is formed by combining predictions from three machine learning algorithms: Decision Tree, Extreme Gradient Boosting, and k-nearest neighbor. A soft voting method is applied, considering the prediction probability of each model and assigning the final prediction based on the average of the overall probabilities. This research evaluates the approach using a dataset that contains various botnet attack scenarios, including decentralized attacks. Experimental results show excellent and consistent performance of the VotingClassifier ensemble model in various scenarios with 99.11% accuracy, 99.10% precision, 99.11% recall and 99.10% F1-score. In general, the performance of the proposed ensemble method is proven to be better than classification methods with a single algorithm.

articleTitle: A Survey Study of Strategies for Improving User Interface in Mental Health
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Mental health technology aims to transform healthcare into digital. Optimization of user interface (UI) and user experience (UX) is crucial to engage individuals in technology-based interventions. Mental health apps offer benefits such as increased service utilization, shorter waiting times, and improved access, especially to remote areas. However, some apps still face design issues such as confusing navigation and unclear interfaces. Our research systematically reviewed the literature on mental health apps using a systematic literature review methodology, to shed light on considerations in UI development and aspects that need attention. We found that improvements are necessary for mental health app UI development, such as cognitive load reduction, easy navigation, customization options, age-appropriate gamification, and clear and interactive instructions. Important features include user connectivity, anonymity, support for logging mental health developmental cycles, and strong data privacy and security. The findings aim to contribute to developing more effective and user-friendly mental health apps, thereby improving access to mental health services through digital platforms.

articleTitle: Hybrid LSTM-IoT in Agriculture: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: Climate conditions significantly influence agricultural productivity, with regional fluctuations impacting both crop yield and quality. This study explores the significant impact of climate conditions on agricultural productivity and how innovative solutions like controlled environments are being adopted to mitigate these effects. It systematically reviews the integration of Hybrid LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) and IoT (Internet of Things) technologies in agriculture, focusing on their applications, recent advancements, and challenges. We examined 49 articles of Scopus. The research paper concludes with a compelling overview of agricultural themes frequently explored: irrigation and soil dominate at approximately 17% of the analyzed literature each. Equally significant are topics such as rainfall patterns, climate dynamics, network management, remote sensing applications, greenhouse control mechanisms, and evapotranspiration, each capturing around 38.4% of scholarly focus. Additionally, farming practices, crop management strategies, and disease control strategies collectively account for about 19.1% of the studies reviewed. Less frequent yet pertinent themes like robotics in agriculture, efficient water usage, and advanced pest detection methods are each highlighted at approximately 12.8%. Similarly, topics like production economics, framework development, UAV systems, hydroponics, plantation management, and flood mitigation strategies also command approximately 12.8% of scholarly attention. This comprehensive analysis underscores the diverse array of interests within agricultural research, reflecting the necessity of a multifaceted approach to address the complex challenges in the field.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach to Detect Cross-Site Scripting Attack as a Web Application Firewall
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: In this digitalization era, the transformation of services in various sectors, previously carried out traditionally, turned into web-based services, making it easier to access anytime and anywhere. However, multiple threats, including Cross-site Scripting (XSS) attacks, are becoming more complex. According to the OWASP TOP 10, XSS has been ranked in the top 10 for over a decade. In general, defense-in-depth prevention of XSS vulnerabilities will likely involve several measures and rules that need to be implemented in a Web Application Firewall (WAF). In this research, we conduct the detection model XSS attack developed using a deep learning model approach. Data collected through several open sources were combined to produce a new dataset as input training data. The proposed model achieved a 99.82% accuracy value, 99.70% recall value, and 99.78% F1-score value. We also show how the proposed model is implemented on a Web Application Firewall (WAF) integrated with a web application.

articleTitle: Leveraging Social Learning for Improved Cybersecurity Maturity: A Case Study Using the NIST Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This research shows that social learning can be used to increase an organization's cybersecurity maturity level. Using a literature study and case study approach. Literature studies are used to identify social learning's key success factors (KSF) and challenges in general. Then, the case study was performed in the context of assessing the maturity level of information security using the NIST Cybersecurity framework at ABC Software House, a small-scale software development company in Indonesia. Assessment activities are performed through FGDs which then also identify the most relevant social learning’ KSF to increase the organization's information security maturity level. Next, referring to the selected KSF, a process of identifying and mapping social learning’ challenges was carried out. The integration of social learning can help organizations gain better focus and understanding in nontechnical contexts to increase their maturity level. This research highlights that integrating social learning with the NIST cybersecurity framework can provide organizations with better focus and perspective for formulating non-technical solutions. This study also enriches the existing literature on social learning in cybersecurity and offers practical insights for organizations looking to improve their cybersecurity resilience.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Narrative in Serious Games as an Educational Strategy on the Dangers of Smoking in Junior High School Students
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
abstract: This study explores the effectiveness of narrative design in serious games aimed at educating middle school students about the dangers of smoking. The game design process followed the Narrative-Centered Informant Design (NCID) method, which integrates user-centered design principles with narrative. The design also incorporated key pedagogical principles such as constructivism, problem-based learning, motivation and engagement, and continuous feedback to enhance the educational impact. Therefore, NCID will be combined with these pedagogical aspects to create a narrative in a serious game with an RPG genre to enhance motivation, engagement, and immersion. Two versions of the game, “Smoverse 1” without a narrative design and “Smoverse 2” with a narrative design, were tested using A/B testing. Ninety students aged 13–15 participated in the study, which included pre-tests and post-tests to measure knowledge improvement, as well as User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) and Game Experience Questionnaire (GEQ) to assess user engagement and narrative immersion. Results showed that “Smoverse 2” significantly improved knowledge (p-value 0.003) compared to “Smoverse 1” (p-value 0.105). Additionally, “Smoverse 2” scored higher in clarity, reliability, and immersion, indicating the critical role of narrative in enhancing educational outcomes. The study underscores the importance of integrating effective narrative designs, considering genre preferences and pedagogical principles, to create engaging and educational serious games for adolescents.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Coronary Heart Disease Using Exploration Data Analysis and Gradient Boosting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Information Technology and Computing (ICITCOM)
